# Port of lib/pubid/omg/parser.rb: OMG <acronym>[ <version>[<sep><part>]]
# with the beta-label word-boundary guards (a bare "beta" must not be
# swallowed by the part rule). The GLUED CATALOGUE label ("Beta1" --
# capitalized, the /spec/ALMAS/1.5/Beta1 URL segment) classifies into
# the version (the 2026-10-19 pubid#548 ruling); the LOWERCASE glued
# form ("beta2") stays a document part (the DDS ruling, spec-pinned). A
# /spec/ALMAS/1.5/Beta1 URL segment) classifies into the version (the
# 2026-10-19 pubid#548 ruling); a Beta-prefixed part without digits
# ("BetaWave") still lexes as the part — the boundary guard keeps it.
  grammar PubidOmg version "0.1.0" edition 2 {
  digit = %x30-39
  acronym_char = %x41-5A / %x61-7A / %x30-39 / %x2B
  acronym_join = %x2D / %x2F
  acronym = (letter 1*acronym_char *(acronym_join 1*acronym_char)) as acronym
  word_boundary = !alnum_char
  beta = (" beta" !alnum_char ([space 1*digit !alnum_char]) / (space "Beta" [1*digit] !alnum_char))
  version = (1*digit *(dot 1*digit) [(" beta" !alnum_char ([space 1*digit !alnum_char]) / (space "Beta" [1*digit] !alnum_char))]) as version
  part_separator = space / slash
  part = (1*alnum_char) as part
  identifier = "OMG" space acronym [((space version [part_separator part]) / (space part))]
  alnum_char = %x41-5A / %x61-7A / %x30-39
  letter = %x41-5A / %x61-7A
  dot = "."
  slash = "/"
  space = " "
  entry identifier: identifier

  bindings identifier {
    acronym -> acronym (string)
    version -> version (string)
    part -> part (string)
  }


  test {
    accept "OMG IDL 4.2"
    accept "OMG UML 2.5.1"
    reject "nonsense"
  }
}
